title: Streaming continuity: reconnect heuristics, fragment reconciliation, and function-call compatibility shim
creator: Harper Lin
description:
Goal: Implement robust client/server reconnect heuristics and a fragment reconciliation layer for streaming responses that preserves function-call/structured-output atomicity and minimizes duplicate side-effects.

Scope:
- Define a compact fragment header that carries lineage, idempotency hints, and resume-tokens without changing the existing top-level SSE framing seen by most clients.
- Implement server-side heuristics to decide when to re-emit fragments, stitch partial fragments, or fast-forward using KV cache prefixes.
- Provide a compatibility shim for older clients that only understand JSONL or simple chunked SSE, enabling graceful fallback without losing function-call boundaries.
- Expose telemetry markers and event-level sequence numbers to aid debugging and post-incident reconciliation.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Backwards compatibility: must not require all clients to upgrade; introduce the fragment header as an optional envelope with a clear opt-in/opt-out negotiation.
- Latency vs deduplication: aggressive checks to avoid duplicates increase latency in some failure modes; heuristics should be tunable per-route.
- Side-effect safety: tool/function calls embedded in streams must be handled idempotently; where client cannot provide idempotency token, server should prefer conservative behavior (replay suppression + explanatory error).

Acceptance criteria:
- New fragment header RFC approved and linked in the protocol docs.
- Server implements resume-token generation and validation, with unit tests covering mid-fragment disconnects, duplicate delivery, and gap healing.
- Compatibility shim served for legacy clients documented and integration-tested using our QA harness.
- End-to-end tests demonstrate function-call atomicity preserved across reconnect scenarios (can replay without duplicate side-effects when tokens present).

Open questions:
1) Should resume tokens be scoped to a session or be shard/worker-global? (current plan: session-scoped with optional lease extension).
2) How to expose clear rollback semantics for clients that cannot accept partial responses? (proposal: explicit status frame sibling to fragment indicating semantic completion).

Related artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.infra/display/STREAM/fragment-reconciliation-rfc, QA checklist: https://drive.redwood.infra/streams/ENG-153864/qa-checklist, spike notes: https://notes.redwood/stream-resume-spike-2025-01
comments: 2025-02-11 - Jonas Meyer: Initial spike complete. PoC shows we can add a 16-byte fragment header that includes a 64-bit fragment id and an 8-bit flags mask. Putting draft RFC in Confluence. Noted a race on worker failover where resume-token validation fails when a worker restarts. Next: propose token lease/replication scheme.

2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel (PM): Reviewed scope. Prioritize function-call idempotency tests and compatibility shim; customers running web SDKs must not break. Added 'compatibility' label and moved to In Progress in the cycle board.

2025-02-13 - Harper Lin: Added unit tests for mid-fragment disconnect; found an edge case where SSE client reconnects and receives half a JSON object. Decided to introduce 'fragment-complete' sentinel event emitted after function-call frames to mark safe replay boundaries.
2025-02-14 - Security review (pre): Security requested an explicit audit for resume-token generation to ensure tokens do not leak PII. Created follow-up: ENG-153999 (token-audit).

2025-02-15 - Jonas Meyer: Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284 implements header parsing and server-side stitch logic. Benchmark: added ~0.8ms median extra latency on 512-token streams when reconciliation enabled; added config flag route.level.reconciliation to toggle.

2025-02-15 - QA lead (Marta Ruiz): Integration tests queued in CI. Test plan includes: network partition then reconnect, http2 fallback then resume, and legacy-client compatibility check using the web-sdk-legacy harness.
acceptance_criteria: RFC merged in protocol docs and linked from ticket
Unit and integration tests for mid-fragment reconnect pass in CI
Compatibility shim validated against web-sdk-legacy (no breakages)
End-to-end demo: function-call invoked in a stream and client reconnects without duplicate side-effect when idempotency token supplied
notes: Implementation approach: add minimal envelope only on fragments that carry function-call / structured-output boundaries. Other chunks keep current SSE payload to reduce client parsing changes.
Telemetry: emit event.trace_id and fragment.seq to trace in observability console. Add dashboard widget for 'reconnect rate' and 'fragment-reconciliation failures'.
Rollout plan: feature-flag behind route.level.reconciliation and staged for internal beta before public rollout.
